title: Six Flags Struggled Financially Before Parkgoer’s Tragic Death: Dropping Shares, Crippling Debt, More
detail:
Six Flags Struggled Financially Before Parkgoer’s Tragic Death: Dropping Shares, Crippling Debt, More
Dylan Stewart/Image of Sport/Newscom/The Mega Agency (2)
Olivia Bellusci
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 9:00 AM MST 2 min read
FUN
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Six Flags has struggled financially for quite some time.

On Monday, October 12, a parkgoer in Georgia tragically fell out of a roller coaster and died. After the incident, the amusement park's shares fell to their lowest level since 2009 on Tuesday, CNN reported.

The outlet noted that Six Flags stock is worth just $10 a share, even less than in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company has been riddled with debt since completing an $8 billion merger with Cedar Fair in 2024, and has not had a profitable quarter since the summer of 2024. Shareholders have seen their stock lose more than 80 percent of its value.

Image of Sport/Newscom/The Mega Agency

The high cost of living has also not helped the parks as "Mounting inflationary pressure" from gas prices and high borrowing costs "can't help but weigh on the theme park customer," according to research from Citigroup cited by CNN.

Citi analysts revealed a 15 percent year-over-year dip in foot traffic at the parks from April to June. In that same quarter, Six Flags reported a $203 million net loss, far more than the nearly $100 million loss the year before. The company's income wasn't enough to balance out $102 million in debt payments, and it ended up selling seven parks to EPR Properties for $331 million before the 2026 summer season began.

Another hurdle for the company is lawsuits from safety issues. Last month, the park closed the X2 ride at its Magic Mountain park in Valencia, California, and is facing multiple lawsuits over the rollercoaster, which may affect its chances of securing insurance.

BILL GREENBLATT/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency

"Although the company carries liability insurance to cover possible incidents, coverage may not be adequate to cover liabilities (and) the company may not be able to obtain coverage at commercially reasonable rates," Six Flags wrote in its annual financial filing earlier this year, per CNN.

While the outlet reported that Wall Street analysts predict the company will return to profitability in the summer months when it shares its earnings in November, losses are expected for the rest of the year.

Marqeta, Coinbase to Bring Stablecoin-Backed Cards to Businesses

Cloud-based card issuing platform Marqeta (NASDAQ: $MQ) and major crypto exchange Coinbase (NASDAQ: $COIN) have expanded their partnership to help businesses offer payment cards funded by stablecoin balances.

Under the agreement announced Friday, Coinbase will hold customers' stablecoin balances and handle conversions between digital assets and fiat currencies. Marqeta will provide card issuance and payment processing, while managing relationships with banks and card networks.

The partnership will also use Base, Coinbase's blockchain, for on-chain settlement, which the companies say will support fast, low-cost transactions.

More From Cryptoprowl:

Cardano Founder Hoskinson Says Midnight Will Surpass Zcash, Urges Gemini to List ADA

Stacks Founder Warns Bitcoin Security Breach Could Hit Entire Crypto Market

Coinbase Targets Banks As Institutional Crypto Adoption Grows

60 Percent of Community Banks See Stablecoins as a Threat to Deposits, Lending

Crypto Heavyweights Back OKX at $25B Valuation

Businesses using Marqeta's platform will be able to fund their card programs around the clock and offer cards to customers who want to spend stablecoins without first manually converting their holdings into traditional currency.

The companies said the cards will work at millions of merchants globally that accept card payments.

Marqeta already issues crypto-backed cards for Coinbase. The new arrangement will allow Marqeta to extend stablecoin-backed payment options to both cryptocurrency-focused businesses and companies outside the crypto industry.

"Coinbase is enabling businesses to move money with the speed and efficiency they require," Alec Lovett, Coinbase's head of infrastructure products, said in a statement.

Last month, Coinbase also expanded its partnership with Citi (NYSE: $C) to connect traditional banking services with stablecoin payments for businesses. Coinbase will handle stablecoin transactions and convert payments into fiat, with Citi settling the funds for merchants as the bank of record.

Prior to that, the exchange partnered with payments provider Moov to bring stablecoin payment services to more than 1,000 U.S. community banks and credit unions.

These come as part of Coinbase's push to expand its services for banks and traditional financial institutions as institutional adoption of Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and other cryptocurrencies grows.

Coinbase shares are currently trading at around $183 apiece, largely flat today.

Investing.com -- Shares of Johnson Matthey rose over 2% on Friday as Citi renewed coverage with a "buy" rating, saying the sale of its Catalyst Technologies business and the purchase of Cormetech set up the company for earnings growth and cash returns.

Citi set a target price of £28.50, against a share price of £24.62 at the Oct. 15 close. The bank had suspended its rating on the stock for a period. It expects a 15.8% share price gain and a 3% dividend yield, for a total return of 18.8% over 12 months.

For the year to March 2027, Citi forecasts earnings before interest and tax will rise 16%. It expects adjusted earnings per share to jump about 40% to 182 pence, helped by planned share buybacks that cut the number of shares in issue. That is 12% above analysts' consensus, Citi said.

Johnson Matthey sold Catalyst Technologies and bought Cormetech, a U.S. maker of catalysts that clean exhaust from power plants and other industrial sites, for an upfront value of $360 million, with up to $100 million more payable depending on performance.

Citi expects Cormetech's operating profit contribution to rise from about £13 million in the year to March 2027 to about £30 million the following year, citing data centre growth as one driver of power generation investment.

The company returned £1 billion from the Catalyst Technologies sale through an £800 million special dividend and a £200 million buyback.

It has committed to return at least £200 million a year through dividends and buybacks from the year to March 2027, which Citi said equals a yield of about 6%.

Citi forecasts free cash flow will rise by about £120 million in the year to March 2028 as spending on a new UK platinum group metals refinery falls.

Citi said the current share price assumes cash returns to shareholders will fall by about 4% a year after its 10-year forecast period, with the business valued at about five times earnings.

It called that too pessimistic, noting that S&P forecasts output of light vehicles with combustion engines will decline by only about 0.2% a year over 2028-33 as hybrid growth offsets falling pure-combustion volumes.

France and Germany have proposed more flexibility on EU emissions targets for 2030 and 2035, which could give combustion-engine and hybrid vehicles a larger role beyond 2035. Citi said that could extend earnings at the Clean Air division, which accounts for 83% of group operating profit.

Mobileye Global (NASDAQ:MBLY) shares advanced 4.3% in premarket trading on Friday, 16 October 2026, after Citi initiated coverage of the autonomous driving technology company with a Buy rating and an $11 price target.

Citi analyst Michael Ward identified the automotive industry's continued investment in vehicle safety and automated driving technology as a potential source of long-term growth for Mobileye.

The positive assessment came despite Morgan Stanley reducing its own price target for Mobileye to $9 from $10 while maintaining an Equal Weight rating.

Mobileye shares traded at approximately $7.75 following the advance, with investors also looking ahead to the company's third-quarter earnings announcement scheduled for 29 October.

Citi Initiates Mobileye Coverage With $11 Price Target

Citi began coverage of Mobileye with a Buy recommendation, highlighting the company's established position in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and its expansion into autonomous driving technologies.

Analyst Michael Ward said continued improvements in vehicle safety would remain an important priority for automotive manufacturers over the coming decade.

"The global auto industry will continue to find ways to improve vehicle safety, and autonomous technology is at the forefront of improvement over the next decade," Ward said.

He also highlighted Mobileye's experience in developing technologies designed to assist drivers and support increasingly automated vehicle functions.

Mobileye "has been a global leader in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) for 25 years and has extended into autonomous driving technologies," Ward added.

Citi's assessment suggests that Mobileye could benefit from continued investment by vehicle manufacturers in systems designed to improve safety and increase driving automation.

The $11 price target represents approximately 42% potential upside from the reported share price of $7.75, although the target reflects Citi's assessment rather than a guaranteed future valuation.

Morgan Stanley Lowers Mobileye Price Target to $9

The positive recommendation from Citi coincided with a more cautious assessment from Morgan Stanley.

Morgan Stanley reduced its Mobileye price target to $9 from $10 on Friday morning while retaining its Equal Weight rating.

The revised target represents a reduction of 10% from the investment bank's previous valuation.

Despite the downgrade in Morgan Stanley's price expectation, the new target remained above Mobileye's reported trading price of $7.75.

title: Nike Resale Market Share Rises to 72.3% in September as Jordan Brand Leads Gains, Citi Reports
detail:
Nike Resale Market Share Rises to 72.3% in September as Jordan Brand Leads Gains, Citi Reports
Fiona Craig
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 3:03 AM MST 3 min read
NKE
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Nike swoosh on building ©Shutterstock

Nike (NYSE:NKE) increased its share of athletic footwear resale volume in September 2026, with its Jordan brand accounting for most of the improvement, according to data tracked by Citi.

The sportswear company's resale volume share reached 72.3% during September, representing a month-on-month increase of 63 basis points.

The figure was also above Nike's average share of 70.8% recorded between June and August 2026, indicating an improvement in its position within the secondary footwear market.

However, Nike's September performance remained below the 77.0% peak recorded in October 2023, when Citi began monitoring the data.

Jordan Brand Drives Nike's Resale Market Share Improvement

Citi identified Jordan as the main contributor to Nike's increase in resale volume share during September.

The improvement suggests that Jordan footwear accounted for a larger proportion of resale activity during the month, supporting Nike's overall position in the secondary market.

Nike's share increased by 63 basis points compared with August, equivalent to 0.63 percentage points.

The September reading of 72.3% was also 1.5 percentage points above the company's average during the preceding three-month period.

Despite the recent increase, Nike's share remained 4.7 percentage points below its October 2023 high of 77.0%.

The figures indicate a recovery in resale market participation, although Nike has not returned to the highest level recorded since Citi began tracking the data.

Resale Performance Contrasts With Jordan's Reported Revenue Decline

The improvement in Jordan's resale performance contrasts with Nike's recent comments about the brand's financial results.

During its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings report, Nike management identified Jordan as an area requiring improvement.

The company reported that Jordan revenue declined by a percentage in the mid-teens compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

That decline indicates that the brand continued to face challenges in its primary sales operations, despite its stronger position in September's resale market data.

The difference between the two measures is important because resale volume share reflects transactions in the secondary market rather than revenue generated directly by Nike.

An increase in resale activity does not necessarily translate into higher sales of newly manufactured products or an immediate improvement in the company's financial performance.

Secondary Market Data Provides a Separate Measure of Consumer Demand

Resale market activity can provide additional information about consumer interest in athletic footwear, particularly for established brands with significant collector and enthusiast demand.

How does this remote work decision fit into Citigroup's broader direction?

Citigroup is trying to keep a critical market running while limiting physical exposure for staff, which aligns with its focus on operational resilience. The group has been putting money into data, risk and control systems, and this kind of switch to remote playbooks in Saudi Arabia shows how those investments are used in real time.

Does this create new pressure points for Citigroup's operations or funding plans?

Remote staffing in Saudi Arabia puts more weight on technology, payments and trading infrastructure to keep services steady for local clients. At the same time, recent fixed income offerings totaling several hundred million dollars in new notes show Citigroup still raising term funding, which can support liquidity as it runs contingency plans across regions.

The clearest reference point from here is Citigroup's next earnings update covering the quarter that includes October 2026.
